First listed: 2026-08-10 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Private Credit's Clock is Ticking w/ Glenn Schorr & Ken Worthington | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 72](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ekn2WneOEBA) - 2026-08-10
- [Substack: Private Credit's Clock is Ticking w/ Glenn Schorr & Ken Worthington](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/private-credits-clock-is-ticking) - 2026-08-10

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Glenn Schorr and Ken Worthington discuss cash-sweep economics, AI agents, private-market exits, software refinancing and crypto infrastructure. Eisman is skeptical of Schwab cash dependence, Circle competitive position and private-credit marks. The most concrete credit test remains 2027-2029 refinancing, not current redemptions alone. KKR record exits provide an acknowledged exception. Visa evidence supports incumbent competition but also shows USDC cooperation. Eisman uniform 50% private-software mark inference and broad crypto-hedge logic require stronger evidence and clearer assumptions.

Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.

## Framework and tools

- Separate funding liquidity, asset cash flow and collateral valuation.
- Distinguish institutional versus retail distribution and manager dispersion.
- Separate blockchain utility, token value capture and exchange revenues.
- Model both incumbent competition and partnership in payments.
- Examine service bundling before treating cash spreads as pure customer inertia.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Sweep balances, net interest revenue and funding spreads
- Wealth-channel gross sales and quarterly redemptions
- Private-equity realizations and vintage multiples
- Software maturity ladder and refinancing equity gap
- Trading revenue versus volume and margin balances

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts. Glenn Schorr covers large banks and alternatives; Ken Worthington covers retail brokers, exchanges, alternatives and crypto. Attribution follows explicit questions and continuity but is not an audio-verified diarization.
- Recorded July 30; published August 10.
- Captions render SaaS as SAS and agentic as genetic or gentic.
- Three-speaker turns are inferred from coverage and question context; individual attribution is medium confidence.
- Crypto expected-direction passage contains an apparent down/down transcription or verbal contradiction.
- The $20bn hedge-fund claim is unnamed and unverified.
